proposal.title: Define the MiniScribe 4010 HDD assembly for NCC 1982
proposal.reason: Author-selected MiniScribe 4010, explicitly 10 MB unformatted rather than usable capacity. Add one purchased mechanism and one reusable cabled/mounted device; retain the existing ST506 for historical configurations. Extend host compatibility without claiming completed qualification. The $625 OEM benchmark at 1,000 units is a calculation assumption, not foundation pricing. Its October 1982 evidence is carried back to NCC 1982 by explicit scenario assumption; contemporaneous June volume supply and pricing are not established.

after.name: MiniScribe Corporation
after.description: Manufacturer of the selected MiniScribe hard-disk mechanism; procurement terms and system qualification are recorded separately.

requirements.description: Qualify controller geometry, formatted capacity, defect handling, power rails and spin-up load, cooling, mounting, cabling and incoming acceptance before production release.

chapters.description: The {model} supplies {unformatted_capacity_mb} MB of unformatted storage through an ST-506-compatible MFM interface. Formatting, sector headers and defect allocation reduce usable capacity; the released controller geometry must establish the formatted capacity.

chapters.description:
Logix Artemis — base computer is a full desktop built around {processor_id}.

The {expansion_bus_bits}-bit expansion interface supports Plug and Execute. The rear ROM/EEPROM position serves the operating system and the front position serves office/application software. The host provides a dedicated keyed connector for a separately installed, non-hot-swappable video card without consuming a general-purpose slot; buffered data/address, wait/ready and DMA access are provided, but electrical pinout remains open.

Installed RAM must satisfy the selected configuration, and a monitor must connect to a fitted video provider. Cartridges must match both the software platform and their socket role; external application cartridges are supported.

The base computer is supplied without a graphics card. Display capabilities are defined by the card and monitor selected for the complete system.

Two matched 32-bit modules form each capacity bank, selected independently on the shared bus. Fill banks in order; decode and refresh every rank. Replace the population when changing density rather than mixing module types. Cross-host connector and timing qualification remains open. The system RAM limit is {maximum_ram_kib} KiB. No parity or ECC is fitted; adding it requires a separately qualified BOM.

Native ERA/AIONix applications use {application_api_id}. Applications query the capabilities of the separately installed display hardware.

chapters.description:
Logix Artemis PRO — base computer is a full desktop / server built around {processor_id}. The PRO configuration serves as a network server.

The {expansion_bus_bits}-bit expansion interface supports Plug and Execute. The rear ROM/EEPROM position serves the operating system and the front position serves office/application software. The host provides a dedicated keyed connector for a separately installed, non-hot-swappable video card without consuming a general-purpose slot; buffered data/address, wait/ready and DMA access are provided, but electrical pinout remains open.

Installed RAM must satisfy the selected configuration, and a monitor must connect to a fitted video provider. Cartridges must match both the software platform and their socket role; external application cartridges are supported.

The base computer is supplied without a graphics card. Display capabilities are defined by the card and monitor selected for the complete system.

Two matched 32-bit modules form each capacity bank, selected independently on the shared bus. Fill banks in order; decode and refresh every rank. Replace the population when changing density rather than mixing module types. Cross-host connector and timing qualification remains open. The system RAM limit is {maximum_ram_kib} KiB. No parity or ECC is fitted; adding it requires a separately qualified BOM.

Qualified AION 64K×1 grades for 256 KB modules: 64/128 chips for the 512 KB/1 MB shipping capacities. The 768 KB target uses paired 128 KB two-rank 16K×1 modules. Shared interface and full-population qualification pending.
